arks.name: python-core
arks.description: For Python developers: idioms, typing, error handling, data modelling and stdlib essentials so agents write clean, modern Python 3.10+ code.

arks.name: python-typing-strict
arks.description: For teams hardening Python codebases with static types: strict mypy/pyright adoption, Protocols and generics, and shipping typed library APIs.

arks.name: python-packaging
arks.description: For Python library and app maintainers: pyproject.toml, uv-based dependency management, wheel building and PyPI trusted publishing.

arks.name: python-testing
arks.description: For Python developers: pytest fixtures, parametrisation, mocking, property-based tests with Hypothesis and coverage in CI so agents write fast, reliable tests.

arks.name: python-concurrency
arks.description: For Python developers building concurrent services: asyncio and structured concurrency, threads vs processes, free-threading and testing async code.

arks.name: python-performance
arks.description: For Python developers chasing speed or memory: profiling with py-spy/scalene/memray, optimisation patterns, and native extensions with Cython or PyO3.

arks.name: python-tooling
arks.description: For Python teams standardising a repo: Ruff linting and formatting, pre-commit hooks, src project layout and well-built CLIs.

arks.name: python-review-agents
arks.description: For Python teams: subagents that review diffs for idiom and correctness, audit asyncio code, and refactor safely with tests at each step.

arks.name: python-modernization-agents
arks.description: For maintainers of older Python codebases: subagents that upgrade Python versions, add strict typing, migrate to pyproject/uv and clean up dependencies.

arks.name: python-test-agents
arks.description: For Python developers who want more and better tests: subagents that write pytest suites, hunt flaky tests and investigate slow code paths with profiling evidence.

arks.name: javascript-core
arks.description: For JavaScript developers: modern ES2022+ idioms, async patterns with cancellation, ESM/CommonJS interop and disciplined error handling.

arks.name: nodejs-runtime
arks.description: For Node.js backend developers: built-in APIs, streams with backpressure, event-loop performance diagnosis, safe config loading and major version upgrades.

arks.name: javascript-packaging
arks.description: For JS/TS library authors and repo maintainers: package managers and workspaces, library bundling, npm publishing with provenance and dependency hygiene.

arks.name: javascript-testing
arks.description: For JS/TS developers: unit testing with Vitest, Jest or node:test, plus test-double discipline and network mocking with msw.

arks.name: javascript-review-agents
arks.description: For JavaScript teams: subagents that review JS diffs, write missing unit tests and prune unused or duplicated dependencies.

arks.name: node-upgrade-agents
arks.description: For Node.js maintainers: subagents that plan major Node upgrades, migrate CommonJS to ESM and track down memory leaks that upgrades expose.

arks.name: typescript-core
arks.description: For TypeScript developers: strict-mode habits, discriminated unions and narrowing, well-inferring generics and runtime validation at boundaries.

arks.name: typescript-advanced-types
arks.description: For TypeScript library and platform authors: conditional and mapped types, branded types, type-level tests and fixing slow type-checking.

arks.name: typescript-tooling
arks.description: For TypeScript teams: tsconfig choices for apps and libraries, project references in monorepos, correct type publishing and type-aware linting.

arks.name: typescript-library-authoring
arks.description: For authors of published TS/JS libraries: public API design, dual ESM/CJS bundling, correct .d.ts publishing and type-level tests.

arks.name: typescript-review-agents
arks.description: For TypeScript teams: subagents that review diffs for unsound types, design types for new modules, and diagnose broken or slow TS builds.

arks.name: typescript-migration-agents
arks.description: For teams moving JavaScript to TypeScript or tightening strictness: subagents that migrate files incrementally and ratchet tsconfig flags without breaking builds.

arks.name: go-core
arks.description: For Go developers: idiomatic Go, error wrapping, sensible use of generics and module/package layout so agents write code Go reviewers accept.

arks.name: go-concurrency
arks.description: For Go developers building concurrent services: goroutine and channel patterns, context cancellation, sync primitives, errgroup and race detection.

arks.name: go-testing
arks.description: For Go developers: table-driven tests, interface-based fakes and httptest, native fuzzing and benchmarks compared with benchstat.

arks.name: go-tooling
arks.description: For Go maintainers: modules and workspaces, golangci-lint configuration, reproducible cross-platform releases and toolchain upgrades.

arks.name: go-performance
arks.description: For Go developers optimising services: pprof and execution tracing, allocation and GC tuning, and benchmark-driven changes.

arks.name: go-cli
arks.description: For developers building CLI tools in Go: cobra/flag interfaces, config and signal handling, tests and cross-platform releases with GoReleaser.

arks.name: go-review-agents
arks.description: For Go teams: subagents that review diffs for idiom and error handling, audit concurrency for races and leaks, and upgrade toolchains and modules.

arks.name: go-test-agents
arks.description: For Go developers: subagents that write table-driven tests and fuzz targets, and tune hot paths with pprof and benchstat evidence.

arks.name: rust-core
arks.description: For Rust developers: ownership and borrowing fixes, error handling with thiserror/anyhow, trait-based API design and clippy-clean idioms.

arks.name: rust-async
arks.description: For Rust developers writing concurrent code: Tokio runtime patterns, async traits and pinning, cancellation safety and thread-based parallelism with rayon.

arks.name: rust-tooling
arks.description: For Rust maintainers: Cargo workspaces and features, testing with nextest/proptest/insta, clippy and cargo-deny, and crate publishing with semver checks.

arks.name: rust-systems
arks.description: For systems programmers using Rust: unsafe code with documented invariants and Miri, C/C++ FFI with bindgen/cbindgen, and profiling-led optimisation.

arks.name: rust-cli
arks.description: For developers building CLI tools in Rust: clap-based interfaces, user-facing error reporting, CLI testing and cross-platform binary releases.

arks.name: rust-review-agents
arks.description: For Rust teams: subagents that review diffs for idiom and error handling, audit async code for cancellation hazards, and fix borrow checker errors properly.

arks.name: rust-porting-agents
arks.description: For teams moving C code to Rust or hardening unsafe Rust: subagents that port modules behind FFI with differential tests and audit every unsafe block.

arks.name: java-core
arks.description: For Java developers: modern Java 17-21 features, idiomatic immutability and Optional use, and clear collections and stream code.

arks.name: java-build-tooling
arks.description: For JVM teams: Maven and Gradle builds with BOMs and version catalogs, dependency conflict resolution and application packaging with jlink/jpackage.

arks.name: java-concurrency
arks.description: For Java developers writing concurrent code: virtual threads and structured concurrency, CompletableFuture and executors, and memory-model correctness.

arks.name: java-testing
arks.description: For Java and JVM developers: JUnit 5 with AssertJ, disciplined Mockito use and Testcontainers-backed integration tests.

arks.name: jvm-performance
arks.description: For JVM engineers chasing latency or memory: GC selection and container heap sizing, JFR and async-profiler analysis, and JMH benchmarks.

arks.name: java-review-agents
arks.description: For Java teams: subagents that review diffs for nulls, leaks and concurrency bugs, and write JUnit 5 tests for under-tested classes.

arks.name: java-upgrade-agents
arks.description: For teams stuck on old Java: subagents that move a project between LTS versions, repair Maven/Gradle builds and review the upgraded code.

arks.name: jvm-performance-agents
arks.description: For JVM service owners: subagents that analyse JFR, GC logs and dumps to find bottlenecks, and back fixes with JMH-style evidence.

arks.name: kotlin-core
arks.description: For Kotlin developers: idiomatic null-safe Kotlin, Gradle and K2 compiler setup with detekt/ktlint, testing with MockK, and Multiplatform project structure.

arks.name: kotlin-coroutines
arks.description: For Kotlin developers writing async code: structured concurrency with coroutines, cold and hot Flows, and deterministic tests with runTest and Turbine.

arks.name: kotlin-migration-agents
arks.description: For JVM teams adopting Kotlin: subagents that convert Java to idiomatic Kotlin, migrate RxJava to coroutines and Flow, and review the result.

arks.name: csharp-core
arks.description: For C# developers: modern C# features, nullable reference types, correct async/await with cancellation, and clean LINQ.

arks.name: dotnet-tooling
arks.description: For .NET teams: SDK-style project setup with central package management, analyzers and editorconfig, testing with xUnit, and NuGet publishing.

arks.name: dotnet-performance-tuning
arks.description: For .NET engineers: allocation-free code with Span and pooling, BenchmarkDotNet measurement, and trace and memory diagnostics.

arks.name: dotnet-review-agents
arks.description: For .NET teams: subagents that review C# diffs, write xUnit tests and analyse performance problems with BenchmarkDotNet and trace evidence.

arks.name: dotnet-upgrade-agents
arks.description: For teams on legacy .NET Framework or older .NET: subagents that migrate to modern .NET, upgrade versions and review the migrated code.

arks.name: c-programming
arks.description: For C developers: memory-safety discipline, sanitizers and static analysis, Make/CMake/Meson builds, stable API design and fuzzing.

arks.name: c-review-agents
arks.description: For C maintainers: subagents that review diffs for memory-safety bugs, triage sanitizer and fuzzer findings, and modernise legacy builds.

arks.name: embedded-c

arks.name: cpp-performance-tuning
arks.description: For C++ engineers optimising latency or throughput: cache-aware data layout, allocation strategies, profiling with perf and microbenchmarks.

arks.name: cpp-review-agents
arks.description: For C++ teams: subagents that review diffs for lifetime and UB bugs, modernise legacy C++, fix CMake builds and add tests.

arks.name: swift-core
arks.description: For Swift developers: idiomatic Swift, ARC memory management, Swift Package Manager and Swift Testing.

arks.name: swift-strict-concurrency

arks.name: ruby-agents
arks.description: For Ruby teams: subagents that review diffs, upgrade Ruby versions safely and write RSpec specs for untested code.

arks.name: functional-review-agents
